sentences.zh: 你有伯克利的学潮。

sentences.en: You've got riots in Watts.
sentences.zh: 你有瓦茨的骚乱。

sentences.en: You have the white backlash in suburbia that propelled Reagan in.
sentences.zh: 你有推动里根上台的郊区白人反弹。

sentences.en: So you can tell the whole story of 60s America through the state of California.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以通过加州这个州讲述整个60年代美国的故事。

sentences.en: California also sends the most delegates to the Democratic Convention, I think something like 174.
sentences.zh: 加州向民主党全国代表大会派遣的代表人数也是最多的，我想大约有174名。

sentences.en: So what is that?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么？

sentences.en: About eight or nine times New Hampshire, where McCarthy had started his campaign.
sentences.zh: 大约是麦卡锡开始竞选的新罕布什尔州的八九倍。

sentences.en: The timetable of the primaries now is so compressed that it's basically a two-week campaign.
sentences.zh: 现在初选的时间表如此紧凑，基本上就是一场两周的竞选。

sentences.en: And it's one of the most anticipated and keenly followed primary campaigns in American history.
sentences.zh: 这是美国历史上最受期待、最受关注的初选之一。

sentences.en: Because what both candidates are doing is they both double down on their appeal.
sentences.zh: 因为两位候选人都在加倍强化自己的诉求。

sentences.en: McCarthy in the TV studios, very reasoned, very calm, goes to the college campuses, quoting Catholic writers of the 1910s that no one's ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡在电视演播室里，非常理性、冷静，去大学校园，引用没人听过的1910年代天主教作家的作品。

sentences.en: But I can't imagine that being popular with the freaks.
sentences.zh: 但我无法想象这在怪咖们中间会受欢迎。

sentences.en: No, I don't think the freaks, not the freaks, but the sort of slightly squarer students, maybe only a little bit squarer, but students who are idealistic.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为怪咖们——不是怪咖，而是那些稍微有点保守的学生，也许只保守一点点，但那些有理想的学生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Students who are dreamers.
sentences.zh: 那些梦想家学生。

sentences.en: They like the idea of this romantic underdog, a cerebral, serious person, you know, who quotes, who writes poems and is interested in philosophy.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢这种浪漫的弱者形象，一个理智、严肃的人，你知道，会写诗、对哲学感兴趣的人。

sentences.en: But at the Ferry Freak Brothers, they're breaking for Bobby, are they?
sentences.zh: 但那些“怪胎兄弟”们，他们支持鲍比吗？

sentences.en: Well, so what Bobby does, his aides say to him, do you want to row back a little bit on going all in on these massive rallies in scruffy areas and things?
sentences.zh: 嗯，鲍比的做法是，他的助手对他说，你是不是该稍微收敛一点，别在那些破旧地区搞大规模集会了？

sentences.en: Is this really a wise strategy?
sentences.zh: 这真的是明智的策略吗？

sentences.en: And he says, no, no, this is what I do.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，不，这就是我的风格。

sentences.en: So he goes all in on massive rallies, goes to poor areas of cities.
sentences.zh: 所以他全力以赴搞大规模集会，深入城市的贫困地区。

sentences.en: He's got big black crowds.
sentences.zh: 他拥有庞大的黑人支持群体。

sentences.en: And one headline at the time said it was basically a contest between an evangelist and a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 当时的一个头条新闻说，这基本上是传教士和哲学家之间的较量。

sentences.en: I think there's some truth in that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这有一定的道理。

sentences.en: That captures the kind of temperamental difference.
sentences.zh: 这抓住了他们性格上的差异。

sentences.en: Of course, if you're a real freak, Tom, you wouldn't go to either, would you?
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你是个真正的怪咖，汤姆，你哪边都不会去，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, do you go to political rally if you're a-
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你是个……你会去参加政治集会吗？

sentences.en: No, just stick it to the man.
sentences.zh: 不，只会去反抗体制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: By, yeah, spliffing up, taking LSD.
sentences.zh: 通过抽大麻、嗑LSD之类的。

sentences.en: A sign of how exciting the campaign is that they have a TV debate, which is actually quite boring, because they don't really disagree about anything,
sentences.zh: 竞选有多激烈的一个标志是，他们进行了一场电视辩论，其实挺无聊的，因为他们对任何事情都没有真正的分歧，

sentences.en: which is watched by 32 million people.
sentences.zh: 有3200万人观看了这场辩论。

sentences.en: So a huge audience for a debate in one primary, in one state, among supporters of one party.
sentences.zh: 对于一个州、一个党派内部的初选辩论来说，观众人数非常庞大。

sentences.en: They have a disagreement about how they're going to break up the ghettos.
sentences.zh: 他们对如何拆除贫民窟有分歧。

sentences.en: Kennedy says you have to take jobs and housing and stuff into the ghettos.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪说，你必须把工作、住房之类的资源带进贫民窟。

sentences.en: McCarthy says, no, that's kind of apartheid.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡说，不，那有点像种族隔离。

sentences.en: You have to kind of break them up and then have an argument about that.
sentences.zh: 你必须把它们拆散，然后他们就此争论不休。

sentences.en: Kennedy says, what, you're going to take all these black people and move them out into Orange County?
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪说，什么，你要把这些黑人全部搬到奥兰治县去吗？

sentences.en: It was very suburban, very conservative.
sentences.zh: 那里非常郊区化，非常保守。

sentences.en: And lots of people say, oh, gosh, that's a terrible dog whistle.
sentences.zh: 很多人说，天哪，那是个可怕的政治暗示。

sentences.en: But actually, what's so fascinating about this campaign, which is so embittered, so dramatic, is that it is pure vibes.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这场竞选之所以如此迷人，如此痛苦，如此戏剧化，是因为它纯粹是靠氛围。

sentences.en: So it's like the Roman Republic.
sentences.zh: 这就像罗马共和国。

sentences.en: It's totally the Roman Republic.
sentences.zh: 完全就是罗马共和国。

sentences.en: I was thinking of this while reading about it just now.
sentences.zh: 我刚才读到相关内容时也在想这个。

sentences.en: What's the optimates and the populares?
sentences.zh: 什么是“贵族派”和“平民派”？

sentences.en: So the people who think they are the representatives of the old privileged class, restrained, sober, cerebral, and then the other people who are sort of part of the mob.
sentences.zh: 那些认为自己是旧特权阶级代表的人，克制、清醒、理智，然后是另一群人，算是暴民的一部分。

sentences.en: Is that the distinction?
sentences.zh: 区别是这个吗？

sentences.en: Well, no, not quite.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不完全是。

sentences.en: But yes, appealing over the heads of the traditional elites.
sentences.zh: 但确实，他们都在越过传统精英直接向民众呼吁。

sentences.en: Yeah, a sort of populist and a patrician.
sentences.zh: 是的，一种民粹主义者和贵族。

sentences.en: It's about style rather than about, well, they're both elite.
sentences.zh: 这更多是关于风格，而不是关于……好吧，他们都是精英。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这才是重点。

sentences.en: Well, which you could say about these two senators, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这两位参议员都可以这么说，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's a good parallel.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这是一个很好的类比。

sentences.en: So I think that is a good parallel.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个很好的类比。

sentences.en: Anyway, we get to the last full day of campaigning, the 3rd of June.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们到了竞选的最后一个完整日，6月3日。

sentences.en: That day, Robert Kennedy traveled 1,200 miles.
sentences.zh: 那天，罗伯特·肯尼迪行程1200英里。

sentences.en: He went from Los Angeles to San Francisco, then back down to Long Beach, to Watts, to San Diego, then back to Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 他从洛杉矶飞往旧金山，然后回到长滩，去瓦茨，去圣地亚哥，最后回到洛杉矶。

sentences.en: Massive rallies, pressing the flesh.
sentences.zh: 大规模集会，与民众握手。

sentences.en: He's giving these speeches about his two big issues, which are the Vietnam War and poverty in America.
sentences.zh: 他发表了关于他两个重大议题的演讲，即越南战争和美国的贫困问题。

sentences.en: He is absolutely shattered.
sentences.zh: 他已经彻底精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: His hands are covered with blood.
sentences.zh: 他的手上沾满了血。

sentences.en: They're very badly bruised.
sentences.zh: 伤痕累累。

sentences.en: He's shaking so many hands.
sentences.zh: 他握了太多人的手。

sentences.en: He's, in fact, been advised to stop shaking hands because he's literally shaking hundreds, if not thousands.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他被建议停止握手，因为他握的手数以百计，甚至数以千计。

sentences.en: I've never heard of that happening.
sentences.zh: 我从没听说过这种事。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: Hands bleeding because you're shaking hands so much.
sentences.zh: 因为握手太多，手都握出血了。

sentences.en: But think about it.
sentences.zh: 但你想想看。

sentences.en: If you see the footage of his rallies...
sentences.zh: 如果你看他集会的录像……

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是啊，当然。

sentences.en: I see he's kind of reaching out and pumping in the Kennedy way.
sentences.zh: 我看到他那种伸出手、像肯尼迪那样挥舞的样子。

sentences.en: Camelot shake.
sentences.zh: 卡米洛特的挥手。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: But it's very different from his brother's rallies, which are much more controlled.
sentences.zh: 但这和他兄弟的集会非常不同，他兄弟的集会要克制得多。

sentences.en: There's a frenzied, you know, very 1968, a frenzied, frenetic atmosphere to this.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种狂热的、你知道的，非常1968年的、狂乱而躁动的氛围。

sentences.en: People screaming and shouting.
sentences.zh: 人们尖叫呐喊。

sentences.en: It's hot, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，天气很热。

sentences.en: It's California in June.
sentences.zh: 这是六月的加州。

sentences.en: You know, the whole thing is really overwrought.
sentences.zh: 你知道，整个场面真的太夸张了。

sentences.en: Shea Stadium vibe.
sentences.zh: 谢伊体育场的那种氛围。

sentences.en: Very much.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Candlestick Park.
sentences.zh: 烛台公园。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's lost his voice.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他嗓子都喊哑了。

sentences.en: He's on the verge of collapse.
sentences.zh: 他已处于崩溃边缘。

sentences.en: His team are very worried now about the danger of assassination.
sentences.zh: 他的团队现在非常担心暗杀的危险。

sentences.en: They've had a lot of death threats.
sentences.zh: 他们收到了很多死亡威胁。

sentences.en: Ethel is very frightened.
sentences.zh: 埃塞尔非常害怕。

sentences.en: What's worse is they have terrible relations with the local police in California because the boss in Los Angeles is a guy called Sam Yorty, is not a Kennedy ally by any means.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，他们与加州当地警方的关系非常糟糕，因为洛杉矶的警察局长是个叫萨姆·约蒂的人，他绝不是肯尼迪的盟友。

sentences.en: Their relations with the local police department, the LAPD, are very bad.
sentences.zh: 他们与当地警察局，即洛杉矶警察局的关系非常恶劣。

sentences.en: The Kennedy people said the LAPD refused to help us.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪的人说洛杉矶警察局拒绝帮助我们。

sentences.en: The LAPD guys said afterwards, actually, the problem was the Kennedy people were arrogant and they wouldn't cooperate with us.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶警察局的人事后说，其实问题在于肯尼迪的人太傲慢了，他们不愿与我们合作。

sentences.en: Kennedy's own biographer, Larry Tye, says, the truth is the candidate himself is part of the problem here, that he's given advice, be careful, don't be too visible.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪的传记作者拉里·泰说，事实是候选人本人就是问题的一部分，他曾得到建议要小心，不要太显眼。

sentences.en: But of course, he wants to be visible because the courage is such an important, proving his courage is so important.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他想显眼，因为勇气太重要了，证明他的勇气至关重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, and to McCarthy as much as to anyone else, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我想对他来说，向麦卡锡证明这一点和向其他人证明一样重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: It's so important to him.
sentences.zh: 这对他来说太重要了。

sentences.en: What kind of presidential candidate hides away?
sentences.zh: 什么样的总统候选人会躲起来呢？

sentences.en: Well, as we will see, Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们将要看到的，理查德·尼克松。

sentences.en: But we'll get onto that later on.
sentences.zh: 但我们稍后再谈这个。

sentences.en: So the 4th of June, polling day.
sentences.zh: 所以，6月4日，投票日。

sentences.en: If Kennedy loses, he is out.
sentences.zh: 如果肯尼迪输了，他就出局了。

sentences.en: He cannot continue if he loses to McCarthy a second time.
sentences.zh: 如果他第二次输给麦卡锡，他就无法继续了。

sentences.en: It's a cold day, unseasonably cold, smog over Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 那天很冷，反常的冷，洛杉矶上空笼罩着雾霾。

sentences.en: The Kennedy menage is staying at Malibu.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪一家住在马里布。

sentences.en: They've been lent the beach house of the film director, John Frankenheimer, who made the
sentences.zh: 他们借用了电影导演约翰·弗兰肯海默的海滨别墅，他执导了

sentences.en: Manchurian Candidate.
sentences.zh: 《满洲候选人》。

sentences.en: Great conspiracy, political conspiracy thriller, of course, of the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是20世纪50年代伟大的政治阴谋惊悚片。

sentences.en: Kennedy, because he's exhausted, he sleeps in late and then he goes swimming with his family.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪因为精疲力竭，睡得很晚，然后和家人一起去游泳。

sentences.en: Son David is almost drowned and he dives in to rescue him, which is a very nice, very Kennedy behavior, Tom.
sentences.zh: 儿子大卫差点淹死，他跳下去救他，汤姆，这真是非常肯尼迪式的行为。

sentences.en: Unlike his younger brother, of course, Teddy Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 当然，这和他弟弟泰迪·肯尼迪不同。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Chappaquiddick notably failed to behave like that.
sentences.zh: 查帕奎迪克事件中，他显然没能表现出那样。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: That's harsh.
sentences.zh: 这话真刻薄。

sentences.en: That's harsh.
sentences.zh: 这话真刻薄。

sentences.en: But I can't argue with it.
sentences.zh: 但我无法反驳。

sentences.en: Anyway, they get back to the house.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们回到了房子里。

sentences.en: Thankfully, nobody has died on this occasion, unlike Chappaquiddick.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，这次没人死亡，不像查帕奎迪克事件。

sentences.en: And the first reports are coming through.
sentences.zh: 第一批报告传来了。

sentences.en: It's looking quite good, but they're not certain.
sentences.zh: 看起来还不错，但他们还不确定。

sentences.en: It's going to be very close.
sentences.zh: 选情会非常胶着。

sentences.en: Frankenheimer, the film director, drives Kennedy into the city.
sentences.zh: 电影导演弗兰肯海默开车送肯尼迪进城。

sentences.en: He takes a very strange, meandering route because he's going to avoid the crowds, which gets everybody very stressed, more stressed.
sentences.zh: 他走了一条非常奇怪、蜿蜒曲折的路线，因为他要避开人群，这让每个人都感到非常紧张，更加紧张了。

sentences.en: They finally get to the Ambassador Hotel at about seven o'clock.
sentences.zh: 他们终于在七点左右到达了大使酒店。

sentences.en: So the Ambassador Hotel is on Wilshire Boulevard.
sentences.zh: 大使酒店位于威尔希尔大道上。

sentences.en: It's in the middle of the great sprawl of Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 它位于洛杉矶广阔的城市蔓延区中间。

sentences.en: And it's a city landmark.
sentences.zh: 它是城市的地标。

sentences.en: It had been built in the 20s and it was famous for this nightclub called the Coconut Grove, which was the ultimate Hollywood hangout.
sentences.zh: 它建于20年代，以一家叫“椰林”的夜总会而闻名，那是终极的好莱坞聚会场所。

sentences.en: Frank Sinatra was always there.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·辛纳屈总是在那里。

sentences.en: Dean Martin.
sentences.zh: 迪恩·马丁也是。

sentences.en: Yeah, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But the whole thing is very faded now, right?
sentences.zh: 但现在整个地方都显得很破败了，对吧？

sentences.en: We talked in the previous episode about Memphis.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集谈到了孟菲斯。

sentences.en: One of the things about late 60s America is that all these old places, these kind of art deco places.
sentences.zh: 60年代末美国的一个特点是，所有这些老地方，这些装饰艺术风格的地方。

sentences.en: You wouldn't find Jim Morrison there.
sentences.zh: 你不会在那里见到吉姆·莫里森。

sentences.en: No, they're kind of faded and old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 不，它们显得有点破旧和过时了。

sentences.en: And this is very true of the Ambassador Hotel.
sentences.zh: 大使酒店的情况确实如此。

sentences.en: Up he goes to Suite 512.
sentences.zh: 他上楼去了512号套房。

sentences.en: He's got all his aides.
sentences.zh: 他带着所有的助手。

sentences.en: He's got banks of telephones.
sentences.zh: 他有成排的电话。

sentences.en: You know, the whole scene that you would expect from a Kennedy campaign.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是你所期望的肯尼迪竞选活动的整个场景。

sentences.en: The polls close at 8 o'clock and the returns are very slow to come in.
sentences.zh: 投票在8点结束，计票结果出来得很慢。

sentences.en: And they're studying the returns.
sentences.zh: 他们正在研究计票结果。

sentences.en: As expected, McCarthy is piling up votes in the small towns and in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，麦卡锡在小城镇和郊区积累了选票。

sentences.en: He is clearly going to win Northern California, the area around San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 他显然会赢得北加州，即旧金山周边地区。

sentences.en: Kennedy is doing really well with the Black and Hispanic voters.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪在黑人和拉美裔选民中表现非常好。

sentences.en: The question is, can he get enough of them in Los Angeles County to offset McCarthy's strength in Northern California?
sentences.zh: 问题是，他能否在洛杉矶县获得足够的选票来抵消麦卡锡在北加州的优势？

sentences.en: It's really nerve-wracking for him and his team.
sentences.zh: 对他和他的团队来说，这真是令人揪心。

sentences.en: The results are coming in very slowly.
sentences.zh: 结果出来得非常慢。

sentences.en: There's computers breaking down.
sentences.zh: 有计算机坏了。

sentences.en: It's a very, very familiar American election night scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常熟悉的美国选举之夜场景。

sentences.en: Finally, we get to about 11 o'clock at night.
sentences.zh: 最后，到了晚上11点左右。

sentences.en: They get good news.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了好消息。

sentences.en: They have won Los Angeles County very decisively.
sentences.zh: 他们以绝对优势赢得了洛杉矶县。

sentences.en: All that time spent on those rallies has been worth it.
sentences.zh: 花在那些集会上的所有时间都值了。

sentences.en: It seems pretty clear he's going to win a narrow victory, perhaps 46% to 42%.
sentences.zh: 看起来很明显他将以微弱优势获胜，也许是46%对42%。

sentences.en: But that's enough.
sentences.zh: 但这足够了。

sentences.en: That's enough, narrower than he would have liked because it keeps McCarthy in.
sentences.zh: 足够了，虽然比他预想的要窄，因为这让麦卡锡留在了竞争中。

sentences.en: But he's now got the big mo.
sentences.zh: 但他现在有了巨大的势头。

sentences.en: Well, or has he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: This is the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: At this moment, in his suite, people are poring over delegate counts.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，在他的套房里，人们正在仔细研究代表人数。

sentences.en: They cannot be sure exactly how the delegates are going to go at the convention.
sentences.zh: 他们无法确定代表们在大会上到底会如何投票。

sentences.en: There's one delegate count that is shown to Robert Kennedy just before he died that is very bleak for him.
sentences.zh: 在罗伯特·肯尼迪去世前，有人向他展示了一份代表统计数据，对他来说非常惨淡。

sentences.en: They say Humphrey's on 994.
sentences.zh: 他们说汉弗莱有994票。

sentences.en: You're on 524 and a half.
I don't know how you can get half a delegate, but there you go.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么会有半个代表，但事实就是这样。

sentences.en: And McCarthy on 204.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡有204票。

sentences.en: There are others that are closer, but he is still a long way behind Humphrey.
sentences.zh: 还有其他更接近的统计，但他仍然远远落后于汉弗莱。

sentences.en: Also, the polls show, counterintuitively to people who have drunk deep of the romance of the 60s, Humphrey is still by far the preferred choice of registered Democrats.
sentences.zh: 此外，民调显示，对于那些沉醉于60年代浪漫情怀的人来说，这可能违反直觉，但汉弗莱仍然是注册民主党人远为偏好的选择。

sentences.en: They know him.
sentences.zh: 他们了解他。

sentences.en: He's the party man.
sentences.zh: 他是党内的人。

sentences.en: Everybody likes him.
sentences.zh: 每个人都喜欢他。

sentences.en: Kennedy only gets about a third of registered Democrats as their top choice.
sentences.zh: 只有大约三分之一的注册民主党人将肯尼迪作为首选。

sentences.en: What's also a problem for him is the next primary is in New York.
sentences.zh: 对他来说另一个问题是下一场初选在纽约。

sentences.en: McCarthy is definitely not going to pull out.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡绝对不会退出。

sentences.en: McCarthy has already held a massive rally in Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡已经在麦迪逊广场花园举行了一场大规模集会。

sentences.en: He's got loads of promises of money from people in New York.
sentences.zh: 他从纽约人那里得到了大量的资金承诺。

sentences.en: His aides are actually quite confident that he can do really well in New York, perhaps win it.
sentences.zh: 他的助手们实际上相当自信，认为他在纽约能表现得非常好，甚至可能获胜。

sentences.en: So at that moment up in his suite, Kennedy is musing with his team.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，在套房里，肯尼迪正在和他的团队沉思。

sentences.en: Shall I make McCarthy an offer?
sentences.zh: 我要给麦卡锡一个提议吗？

sentences.en: Offer him Secretary of State.
sentences.zh: 提议让他担任国务卿。

sentences.en: If he pulls out now and I become president, I hate McCarthy and he's treating me like with total contempt.
sentences.zh: 如果他现在退出，我成为总统，我讨厌麦卡锡，他对我表现出完全的蔑视。

sentences.en: But I will offer him this prized job if he pulls out.
sentences.zh: 但如果他退出，我会给他这个珍贵的职位。

sentences.en: But will he go for it?
sentences.zh: 但他会接受吗？

sentences.en: Anyway, enough.
sentences.zh: 总之，够了。

sentences.en: We have to go down and declare victory.
sentences.zh: 我们得下去宣布胜利了。

sentences.en: He takes a few moments.
sentences.zh: 他花了几分钟时间。

sentences.en: He has a little cigar.
sentences.zh: 他抽了一根小雪茄。

sentences.en: He's sitting there on the floor of his suite.
sentences.zh: 他坐在套房的地板上。

sentences.en: Very Robert Kennedy, 1968.
sentences.zh: 非常罗伯特·肯尼迪，1968年。

sentences.en: Very groovy.
sentences.zh: 非常时髦。

sentences.en: Cross-legged on the floor, smoking a cigar.
sentences.zh: 盘腿坐在地板上，抽着雪茄。

sentences.en: And what's even groovier is they then go down and sing Woody Guthrie songs.
sentences.zh: 更时髦的是，他们随后下去唱伍迪·格思里的歌。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he goes downstairs to the ballroom where all his crowd, all his supporters are waiting.
sentences.zh: 于是他下楼来到宴会厅，那里所有的群众，所有的支持者都在等着。

sentences.en: The place is absolutely packed.
sentences.zh: 现场挤得水泄不通。

sentences.en: If you watch clips of this on YouTube, it's unbelievable how they, not only that they've managed to fit so many people into the ballroom, but the platform, this kind of daze
sentences.zh: 如果你在YouTube上观看这段视频，你会觉得不可思议，他们不仅设法把这么多人塞进宴会厅，而且那个平台，那种位于

sentences.en: at the end of the room, is absolutely stuffed with people singing Woody Guthrie songs.
sentences.zh: 房间尽头的舞台，挤满了唱着伍迪·格思里歌曲的人。

sentences.en: So Kennedy pushes his way onto the platform.
sentences.zh: 于是肯尼迪挤上了平台。

sentences.en: He's surrounded by people.
sentences.zh: 他被人群包围着。

sentences.en: He's almost dwarfed by all these people.
sentences.zh: 他几乎被这些人淹没了。

sentences.en: It's an ecstatic reception.
sentences.zh: 这是一种狂喜的接待。

sentences.en: People are screaming and shouting.
sentences.zh: 人们在尖叫呐喊。

sentences.en: It's now two minutes past midnight.
sentences.zh: 现在是午夜两分。

sentences.en: And Kennedy declares victory.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪宣布获胜。

sentences.en: We've won in California.
sentences.zh: 我们在加州赢了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: He gives, you know, the speech that you would expect.
sentences.zh: 他发表了，你知道的，你所期望的那种演讲。

sentences.en: He says, we can end the divisions in the United States between black and white.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们可以结束美国在黑人和白人之间的分裂。

sentences.en: We're a great country, an unselfish country, a compassionate country.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个伟大的国家，一个无私的国家，一个富有同情心的国家。

sentences.en: I'm going to make this my basis for running.
sentences.zh: 我将以此作为我竞选的基础。

sentences.en: We want to deal with these problems and we want peace in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我们要解决这些问题，我们要在越南实现和平。

sentences.en: So my thanks to all of you and onto Chicago and let's win there.
sentences.zh: 所以感谢你们所有人，前往芝加哥，让我们在那里获胜。

sentences.en: And then he gives a V sign, peace, but also victory.
sentences.zh: 然后他做了一个V字手势，代表和平，也代表胜利。

sentences.en: And now he turns to go.
sentences.zh: 现在他转身准备离开。

sentences.en: Now the plan is to go out to a second rally on a lower floor where an overspill crowd of supporters are waiting and then to go into an annex where there's a load of press men
sentences.zh: 现在的计划是去楼下参加第二场集会，那里有大批支持者在等候，然后再去一个有很多媒体记者的附楼。

sentences.en: and there's going to be a press conference in the chaos as he leaves the stage because it's so crowded.
sentences.zh: 因为现场太拥挤，他离开舞台时，混乱中还要举行一场新闻发布会。

sentences.en: His campaign manager shouts in his ear and says, it's too crowded and it's so late.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选经理在他耳边大喊，说人太多了，而且时间太晚了。

sentences.en: We will skip the second rally and we'll go straight to the press conference.
sentences.zh: 我们取消第二场集会，直接去新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And they push their way out through the back of the ballroom through these swinging doors into the hotel kitchen.
sentences.zh: 他们从宴会厅后方挤了出去，穿过那些弹簧门，进入了酒店厨房。

sentences.en: It's unbelievably crowded and in the crush behind him, Kennedy is separated from his bodyguard.
sentences.zh: 那里拥挤得难以置信，在他身后的推搡中，肯尼迪与他的保镖失散了。

sentences.en: His bodyguard is helping Ethel, who is heavily pregnant, off the platform.
sentences.zh: 他的保镖正在帮身怀六甲的埃塞尔走下台子。

sentences.en: But he's got all his team around him.
sentences.zh: 但他身边还有整个团队跟着。

sentences.en: They continue to sort of push into the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 他们继续向厨房里挤去。

sentences.en: They're almost carried along by this great sort of wave of people, a huge mob of photographers behind them.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎是被身后那一大群摄影师组成的巨大浪潮推着走。

sentences.en: The kitchens are full of the kitchen staff who have waited because to get a glimpse of, you know, America's most famous political celebrity.
sentences.zh: 厨房里挤满了厨房工作人员，他们一直等着，就是为了能看一眼这位美国最著名的政治名人。

sentences.en: And as they go through the kitchen, Kennedy is reaching to shake hands.
sentences.zh: 当他们穿过厨房时，肯尼迪正伸手与人握手。

sentences.en: They go through into a kind of corridor, sort of pantry style corridor.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过厨房，进入了一条走廊，那种类似食品储藏室的走廊。

sentences.en: There's an ice machine.
sentences.zh: 那里有一台制冰机。

sentences.en: There's a row of heated steel cupboards.
sentences.zh: 还有一排加热的钢制橱柜。

sentences.en: It's just yards to go now until the room where the newspaper men are waiting.
sentences.zh: 距离记者们等候的房间只有几码远了。

sentences.en: As they say in an American melodrama, the Sunday Times guys, it was like an alleyway in a ship.
sentences.zh: 正如美国通俗剧里所说的那样，《星期日泰晤士报》的人说，那就像船上的一条狭窄通道。

sentences.en: It was like the corridor of the Titanic or something.
sentences.zh: 就像泰坦尼克号的走廊之类的。

sentences.en: It's got naked metal cooking smells, yellow light.
sentences.zh: 那里有金属裸露的气味，还有昏黄的灯光。

sentences.en: It's very kind of unsettling atmosphere and packed with people.
sentences.zh: 气氛非常令人不安，而且挤满了人。

sentences.en: As Kennedy passes through into this room, a radio journalist is asking him about the fact that he's so far behind Humphrey in the delegate count.
sentences.zh: 当肯尼迪走进这个房间时，一名广播记者正在问他关于他在代表票数上远远落后于汉弗莱的事实。

sentences.en: And he's turning his head to talk to this guy.
sentences.zh: 他正转过头去和那个人说话。

sentences.en: At the same time, he's reaching out in another direction to shake hands with a Mexican bus boy, or as you would say in English, a kitchen assistant called Juan Romero.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他伸出另一只手去和一名墨西哥餐馆杂工握手，或者用英语说，就是一位名叫胡安·罗梅罗的厨房助理。

sentences.en: And at this point, as he's reaching out, somebody pushes through the crowd.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，当他伸手时，有人从人群中挤了过来。

sentences.en: And this is a young man who has been waiting there all this time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个一直等在那里的年轻人。

sentences.en: People say he was wearing a blue sweatshirt and he had what they called a sickly expression on his face.
sentences.zh: 人们说他穿着一件蓝色运动衫，脸上带着一种所谓的病态表情。

sentences.en: And the young man is holding a gun and he fires.
sentences.zh: 那个年轻人手里拿着一把枪，然后他开火了。

sentences.en: A number of shots.
sentences.zh: 开了几枪。

sentences.en: How many is contested?
sentences.zh: 开了多少枪，目前还有争议。

sentences.en: There is a huge melee.
sentences.zh: 现场一片混乱。

sentences.en: People are piling onto this bloke, throwing themselves onto him.
sentences.zh: 人们扑向这个家伙，把自己扔在他身上。

sentences.en: Get the gun, get the gun.
sentences.zh: 夺下枪，夺下枪。

sentences.en: The radio reporters are recording this.
sentences.zh: 广播记者们正在录音。

sentences.en: So we have the audio footage of people screaming and shouting, get the gun, break his fingers, get the gun.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有人们尖叫和呐喊的音频片段，喊着夺下枪，折断他的手指，夺下枪。

sentences.en: Kennedy had fallen back against the ice machine and then he's down on the floor.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪向后倒在制冰机上，然后倒在了地板上。

sentences.en: He's still conscious and his eyes are open, but people see there is blood coming out from behind his ear.
sentences.zh: 他还有意识，眼睛也睁着，但人们看到他耳后有血流出来。

sentences.en: Juan Romero, the Mexican busboy, drops to his side and Kennedy says to him, whispers, is everybody okay?
sentences.zh: 墨西哥杂工胡安·罗梅罗跪在他身边，肯尼迪对他低声说，大家都还好吗？

sentences.en: Romero, yes, everybody's okay.
sentences.zh: 罗梅罗说，是的，大家都很好。

sentences.en: But now the blood is absolutely flooding out from behind Kennedy's ear.
sentences.zh: 但现在血正从肯尼迪的耳后疯狂地涌出来。

sentences.en: In fact, what has happened is that he has been shot three times, once in the head and twice in his back.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他被击中了三枪，头部一枪，背部两枪。

sentences.en: Five other people were shot too in the chaos, reporters and campaign volunteers, but none of them injured so badly.
sentences.zh: 混乱中还有另外五个人被击中，包括记者和竞选志愿者，但都没有受重伤。

sentences.en: Romero reaches into his pocket and gets out some rosary beads and presses them into Kennedy's hand and he cradles his head and his hand is now covered with blood because there's so
sentences.zh: 罗梅罗伸手进兜掏出一些念珠，塞进肯尼迪手里，他抱着他的头，他的手现在沾满了血，因为他的头上流出了

sentences.en: much blood coming from his head.
sentences.zh: 太多的血。

sentences.en: Ethel is now caught up with her husband and she's crying and she says, give him room to breathe, give him room to breathe.
sentences.zh: 埃塞尔现在赶到了丈夫身边，她哭着说，给他留点呼吸的空间，给他留点呼吸的空间。

sentences.en: And then she whispers to Robert Kennedy, I'm with you, I'm with you, my baby.
sentences.zh: 然后她对罗伯特·肯尼迪耳语道，我和你在一起，我和你在一起，我的宝贝。

sentences.en: One of Kennedy's friends, who was a journalist called Pete Hamill, said at this point that
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪的一位朋友，一位名叫皮特·哈米尔的记者，在此时说

sentences.en: Kennedy had this strange smile on his face, like he was very...
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪脸上带着一种奇怪的微笑，好像他非常……

sentences.en: A kind of sweet, accepting smile.
sentences.zh: 一种甜美的、接受现实的微笑。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Then there are paramedics pushing their way through the crowd and the paramedics are straight to his side and they immediately try to lift him to get him out.
sentences.zh: 然后有医护人员挤过人群，他们直接来到他身边，立即试图抬起他，想把他送出去。

sentences.en: And at that, Kennedy says, he just says very quietly, oh no, don't lift me.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，肯尼迪非常平静地说，哦不，别抬我。

sentences.en: And those are the last words he ever says because he passes out.
sentences.zh: 那是他说的最后一句话，因为他昏过去了。

sentences.en: So Kennedy is taken out of the hotel and rushed to the, eventually to the Good Samaritan Hospital.
sentences.zh: 于是肯尼迪被抬出酒店，紧急送往好撒玛利亚人医院。

sentences.en: And news flashes around the country.
sentences.zh: 新闻传遍了全国。

sentences.en: I will just say this.
sentences.zh: 我只想说这一点。

sentences.en: McCarthy is in his hotel room writing his concession speech.
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡正在他的酒店房间里写他的退选演讲稿。

sentences.en: And his campaign manager told me that when the news reached McCarthy that Kennedy had been shot, his first reaction was to say he brought it upon himself.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选经理告诉我，当麦卡锡得知肯尼迪被枪击的消息时，他的第一反应是说这是他自找的。

sentences.en: A day goes by.
sentences.zh: 一天过去了。

sentences.en: The nation is waiting.
sentences.zh: 全国都在等待。

sentences.en: People are stunned and shocked by this.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到震惊和错愕。

sentences.en: But it's not until the 6th at 2 o'clock in the morning that Kennedy's press secretary comes out of the hospital.
sentences.zh: 直到6号凌晨2点，肯尼迪的新闻秘书才走出医院。

sentences.en: And again, you can see it on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可以在YouTube上看到这段视频。

sentences.en: Absolutely stricken.
sentences.zh: 极其悲痛。

sentences.en: And he says to the waiting reporters that he has died.
sentences.zh: 他告诉等候的记者，他已经去世了。

sentences.en: In fact, he had effectively died.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他实际上已经去世了。

sentences.en: When he was shot, like his brother.
sentences.zh: 就像他哥哥被枪杀时一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And indeed, like Martin Luther King.
sentences.zh: 确实，就像马丁·路德·金一样。

sentences.en: Now, to compare it with the shootings of John F.
sentences.zh: 现在，将其与约翰·F·肯尼迪和马丁·路德·金的枪击事件相比，一个区别在于，我们毫无疑问地确切知道枪手是谁。

sentences.en: Kennedy and Martin Luther King, one difference is that we know precisely who the gunman was beyond any possible doubt.
sentences.zh: 因为当时人们扑在他身上，拼命想从他手中夺下枪。

sentences.en: Because the people threw themselves on top of him at the time and fought to get the gun out of his hand.
sentences.zh: 他当时24岁，名叫萨汉·萨汉。

sentences.en: He was 24 years old and he was called Sahan Sahan.
sentences.zh: 他是巴勒斯坦人，1944年出生于耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: He was Palestinian, born in Jerusalem in 1944.
sentences.zh: 并不是你经常读到的那种巴勒斯坦穆斯林，而是巴勒斯坦基督徒。

sentences.en: Not, as you often read, a Palestinian Muslim, but a Palestinian Christian.
sentences.zh: 他后来表示，他曾受到40年代末战争的创伤，他的兄弟曾被以色列军车碾过。

sentences.en: He said later that he had been traumatized by the war of the late 1940s, that his brother had been run over by an Israeli military vehicle.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是有可能的。

sentences.en: I guess it's just about possible.
sentences.zh: 如果你四五岁的话，你可能还记得40年代末的事情。

sentences.en: He might just remember the late 1940s if you're four or five years old.
sentences.zh: 他的家人在他12岁时搬到了美国，他在洛杉矶上过学。

sentences.en: His family had moved to the United States when he was 12 and he'd been to school in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 他个子很矮，很瘦弱，是个独来独往的人，一个流浪者。

sentences.en: He was very short and slight and a loner, a drifter.
sentences.zh: 他进出过各种教堂。

sentences.en: He'd been in and out of various churches.
sentences.zh: 他当过浸信会教徒，当过基督复临安息日会教徒。

sentences.en: He'd been a Baptist, a Seventh-day AdventiSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至还当过玫瑰十字会会员，你敢信吗？

sentences.en: He'd even been a Rosicrucian, would you believe?
sentences.zh: 所以这些人都是流浪者。

sentences.en: So all these people are drifters.
sentences.zh: 是的，这有个模式，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, there's a pattern, right?
sentences.zh: 所有的刺客。

sentences.en: All the assassins.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 萨汉·萨汉后来表示，他被1967年的“六日战争”激进化了，那场战争开始于他刺杀罗伯特·肯尼迪的前整整一年。

sentences.en: Sahan Sahan said later that he had been radicalized, as it were, by the Six-Day War of 1967, which had begun exactly one year before the day he assassinated Robert Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 他后来在接受大卫·弗罗斯特的采访时说，他枪杀肯尼迪是因为，引用他的话，

sentences.en: He later told David Frost in an interview that he shot Kennedy because of, quote,
